newsitem.title: USA: US Senate clears final DC spending bill for FY'97.
newsitem.headline: US Senate clears final DC spending bill for FY'97.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday voted 83-15 to give final approval to a $5.1 billion spending bill for the financially struggling District of Columbia in fiscal year 1997.
The House-Senate conference agreement, which was cleared by the House Aug. 1 by 340-91, now goes to President Clinton for consideration.
The bill orders the city to slash a projected $99 million FY'97 deficit by $25 million, to $74 million.
The $74 million figure reflects a compromise worked out this summer by House and Senate negotiators on D.C. deficit reduction.
A preliminary House measure passed in late July would have capped D.C.'s deficit at $40 million, while the Senate's version that month had no cap.
Negotiators finally agreed to a $74 million deficit ceiling. Under the bill, the city would have to make up the $25 million by increasing revenues or by cutting spending, conferees said.
In other provisions, the bill would make it easier for the city to conduct groundbreaking financings aimed at shoring up its financial position, including so-called tax-lien securitizations.
Normally, such activities, once authorized by the D.C. Council, would have to be reviewed by Congress before enacted. The agreement approved today would waive congressional review.
The agreement also would transfer from the D.C. mayor to the city's chief financial officer all authority and control over executive branch accounting, budget and financial management employees.
The transfer would remain in effect as long as the city's congressionally mandated financial control board "exerts authority" over D.C. finances.
